verdict: OK to lend in Hosur auto components, but only to tier-1/tier-2 suppliers with pass-through pricing and tight monthly monitoring; avoid small single-OEM, EV-transition-exposed job workers.
title: Hosur Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Hosur is a tier-1/tier-2 auto-component cluster feeding OEMs; the business converts metal, aluminium and plastics into parts on job-work and supply contracts, and cash turns on OEM schedules and payment cycles. **Value sits in design complexity and OEM approval, not in the machine.** ICRA notes that complex parts like diesel fuel injection systems carry high design complexity that strengthens pricing power [11], while engine-linked parts face obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]. So when a proposal lands, check what part they make and whether it is powertrain-agnostic; if it is engine-specific, ask for the EV transition plan and customer diversification.

## Where cash and value sit
**Working capital is the real risk, not the P&L.** Gross current assets averaged 160-170 days in recent years for a Coimbatore auto-component peer [10], and rating discipline flags Debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75 times as a stress point [10]. Margins are being squeezed by input costs: ASK Automotive reported record revenue but aluminium squeezed margins [5], and Elara expects Q4FY26 auto EBITDA growth of about 21% with rising commodity risks [6]. So when a proposal lands, check the commodity pass-through clause in the OEM contract; if there is none, ask for the last four quarters' gross margin trend.

## What has changed now
**National demand is strong but credit is running ahead of output.** IIP for NIC 29 is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D], while bank credit is +27.0% YoY against output of +19.2%, a gap of +7.8 pp [D]. Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, 9.3 pp slower [D] — a local stress signal. Peer results are healthy: Motherson Sumi Q2 net profit rose 35% to Rs 223 crore on revenue growth of 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4], and Lumax Auto beat Q2 2026 estimates and lifted its outlook [7]. **The cluster is growing, but the state's tax collections say the local base is uneven.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-1 and tier-2 suppliers with multi-OEM order books and EV-component wins.** ASK Automotive's order wins include EV components across braking and aluminium lightweighting [5], and Pavna Industries has completed a new Hosur plant with assembly shifting from Aligarh by end-2026 [3] — that is real local capex to finance. Avoid single-customer job workers and engine-only part makers [11]. Structure with monthly stock and debtor statements, a commodity pass-through covenant, and a Debt/EBITDA cap of 2.5-2.75 times [10]. Take monthly GST returns, OEM payment advices and a 160-170 day gross current asset benchmark [10].

## Early-warning signs
- **Debtor days stretching beyond the 160-170 day gross current asset norm [10] (monthly) -> ask for OEM payment advices and reprice or reduce limit.**
- **GST collections in Tamil Nadu staying negative against India [D] (monthly) -> tighten new-to-bank exposure in the cluster.**
- **Aluminium or steel input cost spike without a pass-through clause [5][6] (quarterly) -> seek margin support or additional collateral.**
- **Customer concentration above half of revenue in one OEM [11] (annual) -> require diversification plan before enhancement.**
